messages:
julius: FYI I noticed a spike in fn_call validator rejects for canary tenant t-42 this morning. dashboard shows raw counts but no context. anyone digging in?
sarah: checked the telemetry stream. reject rate peaked at ~4.2% between 02:00-03:15 UTC. overwhelmingly from one function: `fetch_order_summary`.
amanda: logs indicate `validation: schema_mismatch` fired before adapter invocation, so adapter never got the payload.
rick: we shipped a tighter enum validator in `validators/v2` last week. sounds like the culprit. main problem is the console only lists counts; ops wants to know how many of these caused fallbacks and billing impact.
maya: product concern: users are seeing silent fallbacks to unstructured text responses which changes downstream UX. we need to surface fallbacks per-tenant and example failing inputs.
julius: proposal: console alert when (reject_rate > 1% AND fallback_rate > 0.5%) for a tenant. Alert payload should include top-5 failing functions, validator_version, sample of redacted payload snippets, and a direct link to bisect/rollout.
amanda: agree but we must limit sensitive data. implement sampled payload capture + redaction rules. default sample rate 5% per-tenant, configurable via console (0-100%).
rick: also a billing semantics item: currently we bill on adapter_invoked. Since these rejects happen pre-adapter, they don't show up as adapter calls but fallbacks to text are billed. This hides cost. I propose a new metric `schema_rejects.fallback_billed_tokens` that aggregates billed tokens caused by rejects triggering fallback.
ops-bot: incident created: #INC-4583 - fn_call schema reject spike (tenant t-42).
amanda: security note: sampled payloads must be stored encrypted (KMS) with TTL=7d and access limited to ops+se. Redaction should be configurable per-tenant (regex/field lists) and applied before storage.
maya: UX idea: in the rejects table add two inline actions: `Mark false-positive` (for SEs) and `Request rollback` (auto-creates a canary rollback request with validator_version and reason). That speeds mitigation.
julius: on routing policy: when a strict validator is enabled, default routing should NOT send rejects to a larger fallback model by default. Instead: 1) route to a canary-compatible model variant if available, or 2) return structured error to client: {error_type: "validation_reject", retryable: false, validator_version: "v2"}. This avoids surprise bills.
sarah: small telemetry ask: tag each validation event with {tenant, function, validator_version, sample_flag, redaction_hash} so the console can fetch summary aggregates without storing full payloads.
rick: agree. also add a short-term dashboard column for `billed_fallback_tokens` alongside `reject_count` and `fallback_count` so PMs can see cost impact.
amanda: I'll draft the sampled-payload security playbook covering redaction, lifecycle, and access controls.
maya: I'll mock alert copy and the table actions by EOD and include a quick flow for SEs to mark FP and request rollback.
julius: implementation checklist: 1) telemetry tagging + `/v1/telemetry/rejects/summary?tenant=...` 2) console alert + bisect link + action buttons 3) per-tenant sampling + redaction rules + KMS TTL 7d 4) change routing default for strict validators 5) new metric `schema_rejects.fallback_billed_tokens`. objections?
sarah: +1. one more: sampling UI should show effective sample rate and number of captured examples in last 7 days.
rick: timeline: I'll open RFC PR tomorrow outlining telemetry + routing change. aim to land canary patch next week if no blockers.
amanda: I'll review RFC for security implications.
ops-bot: will ping #eng-platform when RFC PR is open.
deploy-bot: Canary rollout for tenant t-42 paused automatically due to elevated schema_rejects (auto-action).
